quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #21
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: When should you leave more space than usual between your vehicle and the one in front of you?

options.text: On a hill going upward.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a hill going upward.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle when stopped on an uphill slope. If the car in front rolls backward when traffic starts moving, you will have room to avoid a collision.

questions.question: What is the most important thing to do when driving through a curve?

options.text: Drive at the speed limit as you enter, then slow down at the sharpest part.
Slow down before you enter the curve.
Speed up gently before you enter the curve.
Drive at the speed limit the whole time.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before you enter the curve.
questions.explanation: Slow down before entering a curve. Your vehicle's momentum can make it hard to turn. Slowing down first helps you stay in control.

questions.question: In normal weather and traffic, what is the minimum following distance you should keep?

options.text: One second.
Two seconds.
Three seconds.
Four seconds.

questions.correctAnswerText: Three seconds.
questions.explanation: Keep at least three seconds of distance between your vehicle and others in normal conditions. This gives you time to react if another driver makes a mistake. Increase this distance if weather or traffic conditions are poor.

questions.question: What do diagonal stripes sloping downward to the right on a barricade mean?

options.text: Stop.
Go right.
Go left.
Go straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go right.
questions.explanation: Diagonal stripes on a barricade guide you in the right direction. Stripes sloping downward and to the right mean go right. Stripes sloping downward and to the left mean go left.

questions.question: Another driver's high beams are blinding you. Where should you look?

options.text: At the other vehicle's wheels.
At the right side of the road.
At the left side of the road.
Straight ahead down the middle.

questions.correctAnswerText: At the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: Look toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded and lets you see enough of the road to stay in your lane until the other vehicle passes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No left turn.
No right turn.
No turning at all.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right. Do not make a right turn at this location.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, what should you do?

options.text: Always take the right-of-way over a vehicle in a crosswalk.
Do not enter a street or crosswalk if vehicles are coming.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop for you.
Only use crosswalks when it's convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter a street or crosswalk if vehicles are coming.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a close vehicle may not have time to stop.

questions.question: If there are two railroad tracks next to each other, what should you do?

options.text: It is always safe to go after one train passes.
You must always stop before crossing.
After one train passes, check for another train on the other track.
Honk your horn as you cross the tracks.

questions.correctAnswerText: After one train passes, check for another train on the other track.
questions.explanation: Watch for a second train on the other track after one train passes. Do not cross until you are sure no train is coming from either direction on either track.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Traffic signal ahead.
Fire station.
T-shaped intersection.
Left turn signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: This yellow sign warns you about an upcoming traffic light. Be ready to stop for a red light or deal with cross traffic.

questions.question: What is true about a work zone?

options.text: It can be moving or stationary.
It is marked with black and white signs.
You do not need to slow down or pay extra attention.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be moving or stationary.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving, such as vehicles striping lines, mowing, or removing snow. Work zones are marked with orange signs with black letters or symbols. Slow down and pay attention in and around work zones.

questions.question: When a curb is painted ____, it means you can only park for a short time.

options.text: Blue
Yellow
White
Red

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: A white painted curb means you can only stop for a short time.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Speed up.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Intersection ahead.
Four-way stop ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Intersection ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming. Watch for other cars crossing.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop and look. Go if no traffic is coming.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection.
Slow down and go carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and go carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: You turn left from a two-way street onto a one-way street. After the turn, your car should be in:

options.text: The right lane.
The center of the street.
The left lane.
The lane with the least traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: The left lane.
questions.explanation: When you turn left onto a one-way street, complete the turn into the left lane, which is closest to where you came from.

questions.question: Two vehicles reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time. What should happen?

options.text: The larger vehicle has the right-of-way.
The car on the left has the right-of-way.
The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
The car on the right must yield to the car on the left.

questions.correctAnswerText: The car on the left must yield to the car on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right. The left driver can go when it is safe.

questions.question: Your car is in an accident and is blocking traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
Do not move your vehicle.
Wait for police before moving.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your vehicle off the road if you can.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your vehicle off the road if possible. Always identify yourself and help others at an accident scene.

questions.question: When driving in bad weather, what should drivers do?

options.text: Drive faster to reach your destination sooner.
Stay closer to the car in front of you.
Stay farther away from the car in front of you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the car in front of you.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, increase your following distance to have more time to stop.

questions.question: Which statement is true about motorcycles?

options.text: It is okay for cars to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than with one rider.
When passing a motorcycle, you must move completely into the left lane.
You can expect a motorcycle's brake lights to turn on when slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: When passing a motorcycle, you must move completely into the left lane.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need a full lane of space. Your entire vehicle must be in the left lane before passing a motorcycle.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No parking.
Divided highway ahead.
Left turn signal.
Yield.

questions.correctAnswerText: No parking.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers they must follow the rule shown. This sign means parking is not allowed.

questions.question: When you get in a car to drive, what should you adjust first?

options.text: Your seat belt
The steering wheel
Your rearview mirror
Your seat

questions.correctAnswerText: Your seat
questions.explanation: First adjust your seat so you are comfortable and can see the road clearly. Then adjust your mirrors and steering wheel.

questions.question: When passing a parked vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
Expect all other drivers and pedestrians to respect your right-of-way.
Honk to alert drivers and pedestrians to your presence.
Pass quickly to avoid any pedestrians.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly move into your lane.
questions.explanation: Keep space between your vehicle and parked cars. A person may step out of a parked car, come out from between parked cars, or a car may suddenly pull out.

questions.question: What does a single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Dashed lines mean drivers next to the line can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What does the "D" stand for in the SIPDE acronym?

options.text: Defensive driving.
Decide on a safe action.
Dodge.
Doubt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Decide on a safe action.
questions.explanation: The "D" in SIPDE means "Decide on a safe action." When a hazard appears, decide what is the safest thing to do.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive carefully through the intersection.
Turn right or left because the road ahead is blocked.
Stop and wait for a flashing green light.
Stop, then go when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop, then go when it is safe.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means you must come to a full stop. Then proceed only when the way is clear.

questions.question: Before turning left, what is important to do?

options.text: Sound your horn.
Yield to oncoming vehicles.
Swing to the right side of your lane.
Wait until oncoming traffic has a red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: When turning left at a traffic signal, you must let pedestrians and oncoming traffic go first.

questions.question: When you see a steady green arrow at a traffic signal, what should you do?

options.text: Merge into a lane in the direction of the arrow.
Slow down and stop if it is safe.
Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection go first.
Drive straight through the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn in the direction of the arrow after letting traffic and pedestrians already in the intersection go first.
questions.explanation: A green arrow means you can turn in that direction. You must be in the correct lane. Always let vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection go first.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching a railroad crossing with no signals?

options.text: Always stop completely.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will not happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: When you see a railroad crossing with no signals, slow down and be ready to stop. Look and listen for trains from both directions before crossing. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance and wait until the train passes before crossing.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop sign ahead.
Lane closed ahead.
Railroad crossing ahead.
Traffic signal ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic signal ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers of upcoming hazards. This sign tells you a traffic signal is ahead, so be ready for a yellow or red light.

questions.question: Your vehicle's accelerator gets stuck open while driving on a busy street. What should you do?

options.text: Blow your horn.
Slam on your brakes.
Turn on your four-way flashers.
Turn off the ignition carefully so the steering wheel does not lock.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn off the ignition carefully so the steering wheel does not lock.
questions.explanation: If your accelerator sticks, your vehicle will keep going fast even if you take your foot off the gas. Turn off the ignition carefully—only turn it far enough to stop the engine without locking the steering wheel. Then use your brakes and move to a safe area off the road.

questions.question: How should you always think of railroad crossings?

options.text: Safe to cross, since trains rarely come.
Dangerous.
Safe places to park your car.
Places where you must always stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Dangerous.
questions.explanation: Railroad crossings are always dangerous. Always look and listen for trains coming from either direction. Follow all signs, signals, and directions from flaggers. Never cross until you are sure it is safe.

questions.question: When you park uphill on a street with a curb, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the front wheel straight and set the parking brake.
Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
Turn the back wheels into the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn the front wheels away from the curb.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels away from the curb when parking uphill. If your brakes fail, the car will roll into the curb, not into traffic.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, what should you do?

options.text: Proceed slowly while waiting for an opening.
Drive faster than the traffic on the freeway.
Turn on your hazard lights until you are safely on the freeway.
Speed up to match the freeway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to match the freeway traffic.
questions.explanation: Use the on-ramp to speed up and match the freeway traffic. This helps you blend in safely. You must yield to traffic already on the freeway.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Cars in the right lane must slow down.
No left turn.
Merge.
Pass only in the right lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merge.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that two lanes of traffic are about to become one lane.

questions.question: A fire engine is following you on a two-lane street with no emergency lights or siren. What should you do?

options.text: Drive normally.
Stop as quickly as possible.
Speed up to get out of the way.
Slow down, move to the right, and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive normally.
questions.explanation: If the emergency vehicle is not using its siren or flashing lights, you do not need to move. Just continue driving normally.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It is never used on traffic signals.
It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
Drivers may turn in the direction of the arrow.
A green arrow will appear next.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a yellow traffic light.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the same as a yellow light. Slow down and get ready for a red light.

questions.question: You must not drive faster than:

options.text: The posted speed limit.
A speed that is reasonable and safe for the conditions.
A speed safe for the current road and weather conditions.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must follow the speed limit and drive at a speed that is safe for the area, traffic, pedestrians, weather, road condition, and light. Always drive at a safe speed for the situation.

questions.question: When traffic lights are horizontal, where is the yellow light?

options.text: On the right.
In the middle.
On the left.
On a separate signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: In the middle.
questions.explanation: On horizontal traffic lights, red is on the left, yellow is in the middle, and green is on the right.

questions.question: Regulatory signs are usually what color?

options.text: White
Blue
Green
Orange

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are usually white with black markings. You must always obey these signs.

questions.question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you do?

options.text: Overcorrect.
Turn your steering wheel into traffic.
Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
Release the steering wheel.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your steering wheel in the direction of the skid.
questions.explanation: Stay calm if your vehicle skids. Steer the wheel in the direction the back of the car is sliding.

questions.question: When can you not cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When it would interfere with other traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is broken down.
When passing to the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would interfere with other traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes if you can do it safely without interfering with other traffic.
